headline: High: Open Interpreter’s default filesystem and shell access can conflict with Argo Workflows’ artifact/workspace handling, creating data leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts/parameters into jobs, and Open Interpreter reads local files and clipboard content by default. If Argo-produced content is later pasted or mounted into Open Interpreter, malicious instructions can be executed. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are copied into Open Interpreter via clipboard or mounted files
IF Open Interpreter is run with default confirmation prompts or --auto_run
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents
Use a dedicated read-only handoff directory for Argo outputs
Require manual review of any text before Open Interpreter executes it
Run Open Interpreter in Docker or another isolated environment
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all Argo artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress. If sensitive artifacts land on the same machine, Open Interpreter can ingest them and transmit context to model providers. This is a default-dangerous pairwise leakage path, though the exact deployment is not directly observed.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters contain sensitive data on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a remote model provider
mitigations: Store Argo outputs outside Open Interpreter’s readable workspace
Restrict Open Interpreter to a sanitized directory only
Remove sensitive fields from artifacts before handoff
Use a local-only model provider for Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level sandboxing and per-directory ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can write workflow outputs and Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state. Their shared-state path is via filesystem, so concurrent access can corrupt files or git history without locking. The overlap is explicit in the profiles and dangerous by default when both operate on the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify files while Argo is producing artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Use file locks around shared outputs
Make Argo outputs immutable before Open Interpreter reads them
Pause one agent while the other writes to the workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can emit artifacts and parameters that Open Interpreter may treat as actionable input, while Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If Open Interpreter consumes Argo output without verification, a bad upstream result can cascade into destructive local actions. The pair therefore has a strong default pathway from generated output to execution.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is instructed to act on Argo-produced text or files
IF no human verification step is inserted before shell execution
mitigations: Require manual approval for every command derived from Argo output
Validate Argo outputs against a schema before use
Limit Open Interpreter to dry-run mode for workflow-derived tasks
Log and review all command plans before execution
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between workflow outputs and agent inputs

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows is a workflow engine with artifacts/parameters, while Open Interpreter can access the full local machine and model-provider APIs. If regulated data is processed in Argo and then exposed to Open Interpreter, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific certification mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Argo artifacts or parameters
IF Open Interpreter forwards that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared artifacts
Use a local model provider for Open Interpreter
Redact identifiers before handoff
Set explicit retention limits for workflow outputs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries per agent
